tagline: An old stock driveway climbs toward the Red Wall.
intro: From US 20/26 northwest of Casper, the backway takes the old Stock Driveway toward Buffalo Creek and the southern Bighorns, on gravel across open range still used by ranchers. The tourism office notes that a flock of sheep is likelier here than another vehicle. Through Fifty-Mile Flat the land gains height, and ponderosa pines and wind-carved rock begin to appear.
Then the Red Wall comes forward. The route follows the spine of the southern Bighorns before joining County Road 105 along the wall and returning south to Waltman.

moments.title: Fifty-Mile Flat
moments.text: As the road slowly gains elevation across the flat, ponderosa pines spring up from the prairie among wind-carved rocks.

moments.title: Red Wall
moments.text: A long escarpment of red sandstone and shale runs beside the road, with Hole-in-the-Wall, the hideout of Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid, not far to the north.

practical: The mostly gravel backway is passable for most high-clearance vehicles in summer and fall; trailers, fifth-wheelers and motor homes are not suited to it.
